extracted.intended_audience: American writers, poets, and literati; literary critics and thinkers concerned with the future of American literature
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive standards and ideals for the composition and purpose of a new, native American literature—especially poetry—emphasizing moral purpose, fidelity to Nature, imaginative image-making, civic cultivation, and an energetic, reader-active style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character as chief requirement (not mere erudition or elegance)
rubrics_metrics.description: “character will be a main requirement, and not merely erudition or elegance.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary merit is measured primarily by moral and personal character revealed in the work and its creator rather than by superficial learning, cleverness, or stylistic polish alone. Works should evidence substantive human quality, not only scholarly or ornamental skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intense and loving comradeship as a literary ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: “Intense and loving comradeship, the personal and passionate attachment of man to man ... will then be fully express'd.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature should express and foster strong, life-long human friendships and comradeship as a means to spiritualize and stabilize democratic society; this emotional bond is to be a pervasive, counterbalancing theme against materialism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cheerful simplicity, joyousness, and bodily health in tone
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong fibred joyousness and faith, and the sense of health al fresco ... the great literatus will be known ... by his cheerful simplicity, his adherence to natural standards ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid morbid, overwrought, or affected tones. Favor energetic, simple, wholesome expression—works should convey physical and spiritual vigor and optimism rather than ennui, burlesque, persiflage, or passing fashions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of lurid, morbid, or Puritanical gloom
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the test ... shall be the absence in him of the idea of the covert, the lurid, the maleficent, the devil, the grim estimates inherited from the Puritans ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: do not dwell in lurid, morbid, or narrowly Puritanical representations of humanity. Such elements are seen as decadence or regress and should be rejected in favor of more open, life-affirming depictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest aim: moral civilization, conscience, justice
rubrics_metrics.description: “the lofty aim ... is its development, from the eternal bases, and the fit expression, of absolute Conscience, moral soundness, Justice.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supreme evaluation of great literature is its foundation in and contribution to moral conscience and justice. Beyond aesthetic virtues, works should radiate ethical purpose and help promote the moral civilization of society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature must express 'true Nature' (the kosmos) on a grand scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature, true Nature, and the true idea of Nature ... must, above all, become fully restored, enlarged, and must furnish the pervading atmosphere to poems, and the test of all high literary and esthetic compositions ... not the smooth walks, trimm'd hedges ... but the whole orb, with its geologic history, the kosmos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writings should incorporate the vast, multi-scaled reality of Nature—the cosmic, geological, seasonal, and elemental—rather than prettified garden scenes. Nature should be a source of materials, mood, and spiritual insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image-making and imaginative projection (not slavish replication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet ... by the divine magic of his genius, projects them, their analogies, by curious removes, indirections, in literature and art. (No useless attempt to repeat the material creation, by daguerreotyping the exact likeness by mortal mental means.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the artist's imaginative power to transform and re-project reality into striking images and analogies. Avoid literalistic, photographic reproductions of experience; the image-making faculty breathes life and identity into art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art-qualities as first tests: image-forming, dramatic, pictorial, euphonious, plot-constructing
rubrics_metrics.description: “all works of art are to be first tried by their art qualities, their image-forming talent, and their dramatic, pictorial, plot-constructing, euphonious and other talents.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and formal competencies (vivid imagery, dramatic structure, musicality, plotcraft) are primary evaluative criteria; a work claiming first-class rank must show excellence in these artistic faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the work help any human soul? (empathic/spiritual impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The true question to ask respecting a book, is, has it help'd any human soul?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a work by its capacity to aid, move, or uplift readers—its moral or spiritual usefulness. Impact on human feeling, conscience, or life is a central measure of value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral purpose as the deepest measure of greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: “This is the last, profoundest measure and test of a first-class literary or esthetic achievement ...” (referring to moral purpose underlying the product)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond craft and imagery, the enduring greatness of art rests in an underlying moral/intuitive purpose that resonates across time and elevates humanity; creators should aim for this depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate science and spiritualism; harmonize reason and faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets ... will absorb whatever science indicates, with spiritualism, and out of them, and out of his own genius, will compose the great poem of death ... Faith ... must be restored, brought back by the same power that caused her departure—restored with new sway, deeper, wider, higher than ever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should reconcile scientific insight with spiritual/metaphysical inquiry—faith revitalized through reason and modern knowledge—so literature can address ultimate questions compatibly with contemporary thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate civic virtues: fairness, manliness, decorum, self-suppliance
rubrics_metrics.description: “That which really balances and conserves the social and political world is ... the latent eternal intuitional sense, in humanity, of fairness, manliness, decorum, &c. ... to bring forth, cultivate, brace, and strengthen this sense, in individuals and society.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature should aim to foster social virtues—fairness, decency, self-control—strengthening democratic character indirectly by shaping individual sentiment and public morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce native, first-class American formulations (not derivative imitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: We see that almost everything that has been written ... of old ... needs to be re-written, re-sung, re-stated, in terms consistent with the institution of these States, and to come in range and obedient uniformity with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage originality rooted in American conditions and institutions: reinterpret inherited models so they fit the democratic, social, and historical realities of the United States rather than copying foreign precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and composition should be energized, suggestive, and reader-active
rubrics_metrics.description: a language fann'd by the breath of Nature, which leaps overhead, cares mostly for impetus and effects, and for what it plants and invigorates to grow—tallies life and character, and seldomer tells a thing than suggests or necessitates it ... the reader ... must himself or herself construct indeed the poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor an impulsive, vigorous idiom that suggests more than states, invites the reader's active construction, and prizes effect and impetus over didactic exposition. Books are tools for stimulating supple, intuitive readers rather than passive consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject overreliance on past libraries; use them for comparison and self-knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: how serious the danger, depending entirely on them, of the bloodless vein, the nerveless arm, the false application, at second or third hand. ... the real interest ... is not necessarily to mould ourselves or our literature upon them, but to attain fuller, more definite comparisons, warnings, and the insight to ourselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use classical and inherited works as comparative resources and warnings rather than templates to be slavishly followed; aim for a living, native literature that learns from the past but is grounded in present American life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extremes: balance materialism, realism, and abstract religion with science and emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Present literature ... is profoundly sophisticated, insane, and its very joy is morbid ... fear not ... to sound out ... illusions! apparitions! figments all! ... side by side with the unflagging stimulation of the elements of religion and conscience must henceforth move ... science, absolute reason ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fall into morbid sophistication, unbalanced realism, or uncritical abstract religion. Strive for balance: combine material facts and scientific reason with spiritual feeling, imagination, and ethical restraint to prevent fanaticism or icy abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspire to metaphysical and immortal themes (poems of death and the All)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the future ... must arise poets immenser far, and make great poems of death ... The culmination and fruit of literary artistic expression ... are in metaphysics, including the mysteries of the spiritual world, the soul itself, and the question of the immortal continuation of our identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage tackling ultimate metaphysical questions—mortality, immortality, the soul—as central, noble subjects. Even if such works are 'esthetically defective,' their metaphysical reach can secure enduring value.
